title: Sweetness‐independent bitterness suppression of rebaudioside A by sucrose in a cocoa model
content:
Abstract

BACKGROUND

Taste interactions have been a focus of research in recent decades; however, many underlying mechanisms remain unclear. This study investigated the sweet–sweet and sweet–bitter interaction mechanisms between sucrose and 60% rebaudioside A (REBA) in a complex cocoa model system. A split-tongue method was used to assess peripheral and central interaction effects, allowing the tongue to serve as its own control. The study was conducted under normal conditions and under a sweetness-blocked condition induced by a pre-rinse with Gymnema sylvestre extract. Participants (n = 65) were aged 18–35 years and evaluated sweetness and bitterness intensity during each of the two sessions.

RESULTS

Under normal conditions, no discernible difference in bitterness ratings was observed between the sucrose–REBA mixture and their separate presentations on opposing sides of the tongue. However, under sweetness-blocked conditions, the sucrose + REBA mixture was perceived as less bitter than when the components were presented individually.

CONCLUSION

The results indicated that sucrose has a bitterness-suppressing effect on REBA that is independent of sweetness. Rebaudioside A sweetness was blocked more efficiently than sucrose sweetness. Overall, the observations suggest that taste interactions within this model system may occur primarily at the peripheral level. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry.
